primitives.name: Volitional Attention Boundary
primitives.verbatim_quote: The only resistance which our will can possibly experience is the resistance which such an idea offers to being attended to at all.
primitives.assumptions: Attention is a binary act; resistance is a scalar function of ideational aversion.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When R(I) → ∞, W(I) fails to sustain.

layer2.mapping: GSI: belief update P(W|I) = 1/R(I); GSE: attentional state S(t+1) = S(t) ⊕ W(I)
layer2.telemetry: Change in attention duration vs. ideational aversion index

primitives.name: Ideational Aversion Threshold
primitives.verbatim_quote: There are at all times some ideas from which we shy away like frightened horses the moment we get a glimpse of their forbidding profile upon the threshold of our thought.
primitives.assumptions: A(I) is a monotonic increasing function of I; T is a fixed cognitive limit.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When A(I) > T, attention is aborted.

layer2.mapping: GSI: P(avoidance) = θ(A(I) - T); GSE: S(t+1) = S(t) ∧ ¬I
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of attentional avoidance per ideational type

primitives.name: Willful Act of Attending
primitives.verbatim_quote: To attend to it is the volitional act, and the only inward volitional act which we ever perform.
primitives.assumptions: V = A(I) is a deterministic mapping; attention is a scalar.

layer2.mapping: GSI: V(I) = log(P(A|I)); GSE: V(I) = ΔS(S(t), S(t+1))
layer2.telemetry: Duration of sustained attention vs. ideational complexity

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that volition is not a force but a relational act—specifically, the act of attending to an idea. This implies that volition is fundamentally a cognitive operation where the agent's will is directed toward an ideational state. The resistance encountered during this act is not external but internal, arising from the ideational content itself. Thus, the volitional boundary is defined by the aversion to certain ideas, which manifests as a scalar resistance. When this resistance exceeds a threshold, attention is withdrawn. The act of attending is the only true volitional act, making it foundational to both Bayesian belief updates and state transitions in GSE. The duality of the mind emerges as the relationship between self and idea, where the self is not a passive observer but an active participant in the selection of attention. This framework supports a formalism where volition is modeled as a conditional probability over ideational states, and its dynamics are governed by attentional thresholds and resistance functions.
